title: Introduce kernel notarization & deterministic softlink strategy to reduce runtime mismatches
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Our mixed GPU fleet continues to surface intermittent startup/runtime failures caused by ABI/SONAME mismatches and ambiguous shared-object selection when multiple Cutlass/Triton variants are present. This ticket implements a lightweight 'kernel notarization' artifact and a deterministic softlink resolution strategy that: (1) fingerprints compatible kernel bundles at build time, (2) exposes a compact capability manifest alongside each runtime image, and (3) performs a short (timeboxed) capability negotiation during agent init to select a pre-verified libset. The goal is to reduce noisy runtime crashes, speed up recovery, and make rollbacks safer without bloating image surfaces.

Why now:
- Incidents over the past two quarters show ~9% of hetero-cluster failures trace to shared object mismatches or non-deterministic LD path resolution.
- Ongoing kernel upgrades (CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS) make this more frequent as we ship multiple pinned variants.
- Current ad-hoc heuristics are brittle and complicate rollout automation.

Out-of-scope:
- Rewriting the entire loader. This is a compat layer and policy change only.
background:
We currently rely on filesystem ordering and ad-hoc prelink heuristics to pick which CUDA/Triton/Cutlass shared objects are used at runtime. In heterogeneous images (multi-version bundles) this leads to surprising symbol choices, silent fallback to slow paths, and occasional undefined behavior from mismatched runtime/kernel contracts. Previous mitigation tickets added probe-cache and symbol quarantine, but those are complementary: this work aims to make the selection deterministic and auditable by producing small manifests (fingerprints) and a documented negotiation flow used at init.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc (proto): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/GPU+Kernel+Notary+Design
- Spike repo (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/kernel-notary-spike
- Incident runbook references: https://go.redwood.ai/incident/2024-11-kernel-mismatch
acceptance_criteria:
- At least one kernel-notary manifest format defined and parsed by the agent.
- Agent init time negotiation is timeboxed to <= 120ms additional overhead on average (measured in perf CI).
- Deterministic selection (same inputs => same chosen bundle) for staging images in 10 consecutive runs.
- Telemetry emitted for selection decisions and rejected bundles, visible in Console per-node debug view.
- Canary rollout to 5% of Dedicated capacity with automatic rollback on >0.5% new-error delta.
implementation_plan:
1) Define notarization manifest schema (JSON lines, compact): fields: bundle_id, kernel_version, SONAMEs, symbol_fingerprint (sha256), qualifiers (cuda_major, cuda_minor, cutlass_tag, triton_tag), build_time, signed_by.
2) Extend build pipeline to produce manifest + attach to image tarball (opt-in initially).
3) Implement agent-side resolver that prefers signed+compatible bundles, falls back to best-effort mapping if no signed match, and emits structured telemetry.
4) Add deterministic softlink strategy: create /usr/local/redwood/kernels/active -> /usr/local/redwood/kernels/bundle-<bundle_id> and ensure ldconfig paths are ordered consistently; document ordering semantics.
5) Add feature-flag and rollout config in Console; wire canary percent controls and failure thresholds.
6) Add unit tests for manifest parser, integration tests in CI images, and a staging e2e that cycles heterogeneous bundles across nodes.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for manifest parsing and fingerprint verification.
- Perf CI: measure cold-start time difference with/without notary across N=50 runs on p4d and a100 instances. Target: median overhead < 120ms.
- Staging: deploy to hetero-cluster with 3 GPU families; run synthetic load, verify determinism in selection across 100 restarts.
- Canary: 5% traffic routing for 48 hours with automated monitoring of error rate, tail latency, and kernel-fallback counts.
- Chaos: simulate missing signed bundles to exercise fallback and rollbacks.
rollback_plan:
- Feature-flag off: agent reverts to current ordering heuristics immediately.
- If agent-level rollback insufficient: release emergency image with legacy loader (known-good) and drain canary nodes.
- Postmortem tasks: collect failed manifests and add coverage to manifest registry.
observability:
- New telemetry events: kernel_notary.selection_decision, kernel_notary.fallback_reason, kernel_notary.signature_validation.
- Tags: node_id, bundle_id, chosen_bundle_id, cuda_version, cutlass_tag, triton_tag, startup_latency_ms.
- Console dashboard: per-node selection heatmap and recent rejected bundles table.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Manifest signing key compromise => mitigation: rotate keys, short-lived signing with KMS, and add signature revocation list.
- Risk: Unexpected perf regression during init => mitigation: timebox negotiation + telemetry + canary gating.
- Risk: Build pipeline complexity increases => mitigation: opt-in initial phase and gradual enforcement, documented build plugin.
notes:
- This approach intentionally keeps the runtime changes minimal and focuses on artifact metadata and deterministic filesystem layout.
- Coordinate with release engineering to ensure manifest generation is added to N-1 images before enforcing hard-fail on unsigned bundles.
- Consider a follow-up ticket to expose a manifest registry service for central verification across fleets.
